fields.meta_title: Tryout Evaluation Form Builder for Coaches | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a tryout evaluation form coaches score on a phone. The app averages every evaluator, ranks each player, and emails families feedback.
fields.h1: Build a Tryout Evaluation Form That Ranks Every Player
fields.hero_description: Build a tryout evaluation form coaches score on a phone, with every evaluator averaged into one ranked list of players.
fields.features_heading: What a Clipboard Misses at Tryouts
fields.features_subheading: A paper sheet holds one coach's view. Emergent builds the form and the scoring app that puts every coach's numbers together.
fields.feature_1:
Scoring on a phone at every station

Each evaluator opens the form on a phone and taps a 1 to 5 score for the tryout number in front of them. Scores save as they go, so no sheet goes missing between drills.
fields.feature_2:
Skills named for your sport

Describe the drills you run, and Emergent builds a scored skill for each. A softball form rates hitting and fielding, while a basketball form rates ball handling and defense.
fields.feature_3:
One average from every evaluator

Three coaches scoring the same player add up to one number. The app averages each skill across evaluators, and the head coach reads a single total out of 20 for each player.
fields.feature_4:
Check-in that hands out tryout numbers

Players register before tryouts with grade, position, and a parent's email. The app gives each one a tryout number, and evaluators score that number instead of a name.
fields.feature_5:
Every score in a database you own

Each score and note, plus every roster decision, is a row in a database you own. Next season, open a returning player's scores from last spring before the first drill of tryouts.
fields.feature_6:
Code your school can host

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and host the app wherever your school or club runs its other tools. Keep changing it by prompt after that.

fields.usecase_heading: Where the Scores Go After Tryouts
fields.tab_content_1:
From 38 players to a varsity of 14

Softball tryouts at Ashgrove Bend High drew 38 players. Three coaches scored each one 1 to 5 on hitting, fielding, throwing, and base running, for a total out of 20. The app averages the three totals and ranks everyone. The top 14 make varsity and the next 14 make JV, with #22 last in at 15.7.
fields.tab_content_2:
When two coaches split on defense, #31 plays again Saturday

Four evaluators scored 26 players at the Tri-County Hoops 15U tryout. On defense, one coach gave #31 a 2 and another gave a 5. A gap of 2 or more points on the same skill puts a player on a second-look list. Number 31 joined 2 others there, and all 3 play in Saturday's scrimmage before the roster goes up.
fields.tab_content_3:
By score, 64 kids land on 8 even U10 teams

Pinewood Youth Soccer used to let volunteer coaches pick their own U10 players, and one team always came out stacked. Now the app deals all 64 scored kids onto 8 teams of 8 in score order, reversing direction each round. Every team's average lands between 3.3 and 3.5.
fields.tab_content_4:
Each family learns which skill to work on all summer

Families at Gullwing Point Volleyball used to hear only whether their player made a team. On Mar 9 the app emails all 52 families their player's average in each skill, with the lowest one marked as the skill to work on. For Ondine Carrow, that was serve receive at 2.7, next to passing at 4.1 and serving at 3.8.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Tryout Evaluation Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to a tryout evaluation form that turns every coach's scores into one ranked list, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List the skills coaches already judge
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Pick one scale and define its numbers
fields.howto_step_1_des: List the skills your coaches already judge at tryouts, such as hitting and fielding for softball or ball handling and defense for basketball. Keep it to four to six per player, because each one is a tap an evaluator makes before the next drill starts.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Score every skill on the same 1 to 5 scale. Write one line for a 1, a 3, and a 5, such as "fields cleanly on the move" for a 5. Two coaches then mean the same thing when they give the same number.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Collect each player's details at registration and assign a tryout number to pin on. Evaluators score that number, not a name. The record keeps both, and the ranked list shows the name beside each number when the coaches sit down to decide.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Average each skill across evaluators, then add the skills into one total. Set the gap that counts as a disagreement, such as 2 points on one skill, and send any player who crosses it to a second look before the roster is final.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Tell the app how many spots each team holds, like 14 for varsity and 14 for JV. A rec league can instead deal players out by score onto even teams. Either way, the ranked list fills each team from the top down.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Describe it all in one prompt
fields.howto_step_6_des: Put every decision from the first five steps into a single prompt, written the way you would brief an assistant coach. Emergent builds the scoring form and check-in, plus the ranked list behind them. Change any part later by describing the change in plain English.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Score one player twice on purpose
fields.howto_step_7_des: Before tryout day, have two coaches score one player from a practice video using the form. If their numbers land far apart on a skill, rewrite that skill's descriptions from step 2 until both coaches would give the same score.

faq_plan.q: What is a tryout evaluation form?
faq_plan.a: A tryout evaluation form is the score sheet coaches fill in for each player at tryouts. It rates a fixed list of skills on one scale and holds the notes behind each rating. The coaches then decide who makes which team from those numbers.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a tryout evaluation form?
faq_plan.a: Decide the skills and the scale, along with how many spots each team has. Describe them to Emergent's AI form builder in one prompt. It builds the form evaluators score on and the results behind it. The steps above cover each decision in order.

faq_plan.q: What skills should a softball tryout evaluation form score?
faq_plan.a: Score every player on the same four core skills as the softball example above. Then add position stations: catchers get blocking and pop time, and pitchers get accuracy and velocity. Those extra skills appear only for players who list that position at check-in.

faq_plan.q: What rating scale works best on a basketball evaluation form?
faq_plan.a: A 1 to 5 scale with a written description for each number works best for tryouts. On a 1 to 10 scale, coaches split hairs between a 6 and a 7 without agreeing on what either means. An employee evaluation form uses the same trick: every rating names the behavior behind it.

faq_plan.q: How many coaches should score a basketball tryout evaluation form?
faq_plan.a: Plan on at least 2 evaluators per player, and 3 or 4 when you can staff the stations. One coach sees one drill on one day, and an average smooths out a bad rep. Rotate evaluators between stations instead of parking each coach on one skill.

faq_plan.q: What should a basketball player evaluation form include besides skill scores?
faq_plan.a: Add what the coaches need at the decision table: position, grade, height, last season's team, and a short note for each station. A coachability rating, scored like any skill, records how a player takes a correction. Keep the notes factual, since families may ask to read them.

faq_plan.q: How should a high school softball tryout evaluation form handle returning players?
faq_plan.ref: high school softball tryout evaluation form
faq_plan.secondary: high school softball tryout evaluation form
faq_plan.a: Score returning players on the same form and scale as newcomers, with no bonus for last season. Put last year's average beside this year's on the ranked list, and the coaches see the trend without it moving the number. With Emergent, last spring's scores stay in a database you own. Holding every candidate to the same criteria is also how an interview evaluation form works.

faq_plan.q: Should players see the scores on their tryout evaluation form?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the feedback is written for them. A player who sees a weak score in one skill knows what to practice, while a bare team placement says nothing. Share skill averages and a coach's note, and keep each evaluator's individual scores private. The app can email each family on the date the coaches pick.

faq_plan.q: How do I keep a softball evaluation form fair when coaches already know the players?
faq_plan.a: Assign each coach to score groups that hold none of the players from their own current team. Hide the running averages until every evaluator has submitted, and no coach can adjust a score to match a colleague's. Players wear a tryout number, and the name only joins the scores at the decision table.

faq_plan.q: Can a tryout evaluation form be reused for other kinds of evaluation?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Swap the skills and the descriptions behind each number, and the same averaging and ranking work for a debate team or a dance squad. A presentation evaluation form follows the same pattern with criteria like structure and delivery. Emergent changes the form when you describe the change in a prompt.

plan.angle: The top 10 is printable tryout sheets (softball, soccer, basketball, volleyball PDFs, a Pinterest board, a league scoring sheet): every result gives one coach a grid to fill by hand, and none shows what happens when three coaches score forty players and someone has to add it up. This page covers the tryout evaluation form as a scoring app: evaluators score each tryout number on a phone, the app averages every evaluator, ranks the players against the roster size, flags scores that coaches disagree on, balances rec teams and sends each family its feedback.
